scoreNote: Strong-adequate (4.5): a policy response that backs free tuition for needy admitted students while arguing it must be funded with care; two developed examples with analysis, controlled prose on a memorable First and Second skeleton.

sentences.text: Every year, talented students win a place at university but cannot pay the tuition.
One proposed policy is that governments should offer a free university education to any admitted student who cannot afford it.
I largely support this policy, though I believe it must be funded and managed with care.

sections.role: Body 1 — Why need-based free tuition is worthwhile

sentences.text: First, paying for admitted students who cannot afford tuition is plainly worthwhile.
A student qualified for university should not be turned away simply because she is poor.
For example, a gifted student from a poor family could become a doctor the whole society needs.
This shows that helping such students turns wasted talent into real benefit for everyone.
Removing the barrier of cost also makes opportunity fairer between rich and poor.
A nation that educates its talented poor invests wisely in its own future.
To this extent, the policy is both fair and sensible.

sections.role: Body 2 — Why it must be funded with care

sentences.text: Second, however, the policy must be funded and managed carefully to work well.
Free tuition is never truly free, since the public must pay for it through taxes.
Consider a government that promises free education but cannot afford it, leaving universities underfunded.
Such failure shows that good intentions need realistic funding behind them.
Clear rules are also needed to ensure that help goes to those who genuinely cannot pay.
Without careful planning, the policy could be wasteful or open to abuse.
The policy, then, works best when it is generous but also responsible.
In conclusion, governments should help admitted students who cannot afford university.
But the policy must be funded and managed carefully to succeed.
The wisest approach pays for talented students in real need while planning the cost responsibly.
